source_text.Q-1053: CI flake, supervisor-prioritised 2026-10-12. Queue Q-1053 / GH #2399, issue_ref ISS-1053. See task.description.

task.description:
WF-03 Step 1 diagnosis + exact fix design (ISSUE-FIXER, .claude/agents/issue-fixer.md) for Q-1053 / GH #2399, queue issue_ref ISS-1053 (CI flake, priority raised by the supervisor: it now makes other PRs red). Branch feature/WF03-ISS1053SHARDFLAKE-20261012 (from origin/main). Read the GH issue (gh issue view 2399 --comments) for both occurrences.

Failures: test/scripts/test_parallel_shard_test.exs:241 "shard 2 of 3 under admission control cap 1" fails with "partition 7's process exited during its own template build, before producing a ready-file" (CI run 38227698118, loadavg 10.09 on 4 cores); recurrence :274 "TEST_PARALLEL_SHARD SHARD wins over TOTAL and OFFSET (even invalid ones)" (PR #2383, CI run 38263915020, shard 2/3, job 114861236729, nested runner's partition-1 log is missing, load 9.75). Both are green on rerun; on main the test ran green on 7a66381e and 2809e5ff. The tests use stub bash partitions and no BEAM and drive scripts/test_parallel.sh (and possibly scripts/timed_test.sh) with a stub mix.

Acceptance (queue): (1) the cause of the early exit is diagnosed from a captured partition log, or the capture is added so the next occurrence leaves one; (2) a KEEP_LOGS-style capture (name chosen by the implementer; check scripts/test_parallel.sh for an existing TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS or similar) keeps each stub partition's log when a partition exits without its ready-file, and the failure message names the kept log path; (3) the test's wait remains bounded, failure still reported when a ready-file never appears; (4) assertions on the ready-file-to-global-index pairing unchanged; (5) five consecutive local runs of the test under CPU load recorded with real output. The supervisor adds: look at ALL tests in that file that read the nested runner's partition log or wait on ready-files, not just :241 and :274.

Do: read test/scripts/test_parallel_shard_test.exs fully and scripts/test_parallel.sh (partition spawn, ready-file, template build, log paths, cleanup trap, admission control, the SHARD/TOTAL/OFFSET handling). Find a plausible mechanism for "process exited before ready-file / partition log missing" under load that is NOT just "slow machine" (e.g. a timing assumption, a cleanup trap that deletes the log dir before the test reads it, a shared tmp path or partition-number collision between the nested runner and a concurrently running real runner on the same host or CI shard, a wait deadline too short, the stub killed by the harness's own timeout or process-group signal, set -e/pipefail interplay, a mktemp dir removed by the test's on_exit while the stub still runs). Prove or refute each candidate by reading code and, where safe, by a controlled local reproduction (stress: run the single test file in a loop with CPU burners, for example 4 parallel busy loops, 20+ iterations; keep ALL output). If a root cause can be shown, design the minimal fix (production script change only if the script is at fault, else test-only). In every case design the capture: keep logs on failure with the path in the failure message. Check docs/anti-patterns.md.

Deliver: root cause (or ranked hypotheses with the evidence), the exact design (files, code shape, wait bounds, messages), the stress-run protocol, a mutant list (a regression of the fix that must fail the new or changed test), risks. Do NOT write the implementation. Local issue id: use ISS-1062 (ISS-1059 is taken, ISS-1061 is used by the open branch feature/WF03-ISS1054DBGUARD-20261012); verify it is free (docs/issues, git ls-remote --heads origin, queue max ref is ISS-1060) and create docs/issues/<id>.yaml with queue_ref Q-1053, github_ref GH-2399 (schema of docs/issues/ISS-1058.yaml).

Mix is allowed ONLY under the machine-wide mutex (one BEAM at a time; one acquisition per mix invocation, so a stress loop acquires per iteration): L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$L")"; until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 20; done; trap 'rmdir "$L" 2>/dev/null' EXIT; cd /c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow && LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test <ONE mix invocation>. A throwaway postgres:16 on 5499 is needed only if the test touches the DB (check; docker run -d --rm --name pg1053 -e POSTGRES_USER=letflow -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=letflow -e POSTGRES_DB=letflow_dev -p 5499:5432 postgres:16; remove afterwards). Foreground only; no Monitors.

Result into this handoff (COMPLETED, result.status PASS/FAIL, no BOM, LF, artifacts_out under result, no self-reference); pull --rebase, commit, push with bounded retry on github resolve failures; message ends: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

result.summary:
LOCAL ID: ISS-1062 (docs/issues/ISS-1062.yaml, queue_ref Q-1053, github_ref GH-2399; verified free in docs/issues, origin heads, origin/main). Registry lookup: ISS-0698/0917/0921 touch the same script areas, none matches these symptoms; no resolved recurrence. VERDICT: not one flake but FOUR independent defects behind the "test_parallel family" failures. Three are in scripts/test_parallel.sh (the production script is at fault; tests only expose them with instantly-exiting stubs), one is a test wall-clock window. Reproduced in a linux container (postgres:16 image, bash 5.2.37, --cpus 4, 12 busy loops) by driving the REAL script with the same stub mix/psql as the test (stub copied from test_parallel_shard_test.exs write_stubs, same env). No BEAM, no DB, no mix was run, so the mix mutex was not needed. RC-A (shard :274; mechanism PROVEN) - the EXIT trap runs in a killed watchdog subshell and rm -rf's the run's tmp_dir. CI evidence (job 114861236729): "phase elapsed=0s", "grep: .../partition-N.log: No such file or directory" for all 4, "partition N has no Result: line ... exit=0", "elapsed=0s", "0/4 partitions reported", then "preserving (exit_code=1)". Exit 0 plus a missing log means the log was created and then deleted after the stub finished. Cause: Step 2 starts one watchdog per partition as "( sleep ...; kill ... ) &" and Step 3 kills its process group (kill -- -pid) the moment the partition's wait returns, which with stubs is milliseconds. A bash subshell child receiving a fatal signal in the window between fork() and bash resetting its inherited handlers runs the PARENT's EXIT trap (cleanup_tmp_dir) via termsig_handler, with $? = the parent's last status 0, so the "exit_code -eq 0 and no KEEP_LOGS" branch executes rm -rf "$tmp_dir" under the running parent (it also runs the "reap still-alive partitions" loop). Evidence: minimal reproducer (EXIT trap + set -m + "( sleep 5 ) &" + immediate kill): the subshell ran the trap in 214/1000 iterations (linux), 36/100 at delay 0, 0/100 at delays >= 5 ms (so the window is only the fork gap). Natural reproduction on the unmodified script, scenario shard 1/3 cap 4, 12 burners: LOGS-MISSING 1/300 (iter 90); scenario A 0/150. Mutant that kills the watchdog right after fork: 15/25 runs reproduce the CI signature; the same mutant plus a guard as first statement after "local exit_code=$?" in cleanup_tmp_dir ([ "${BASHPID:-$$}" = "$_tp_main_pid" ] || return 0, with _tp_main_pid=$$ set before "trap cleanup_tmp_dir EXIT"): 25/25 green. Production exposure: practically none (a real partition lives minutes, the kill is never in the fork window), but the trap is latently unsafe in every subshell. NOTE: a capture knob would MASK this bug: do not set TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS in the nested env (it skips the rm), the regression test needs it unset. RC-B (shard :241; mechanism PROVEN by window-widening; natural occurrence not reproduced, 0/150 under load) - TOCTOU in poll_template_ready_dir (scripts/test_parallel.sh ~L621-640). It tests [ -e partition-N.ready ] and only then kill -0 pid. A stub that writes the ready-file and exits between the two builtins (the stub does both within ms; a real mix lives minutes so production never hits it) is reported as "partition N's process exited during its own template build, before producing a ready-file" and exit 1. Under load the poller is preempted between the two builtins for the stub's whole remaining life. Mutant: sleep 0.3 between the two (elif ! { sleep 0.3; kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; }) -> scenario cap 1 shard 2/3 fails 6/6 with the exact CI message (partition 5 here, 7 in CI). Fix variants verified: re-test the ready-file after the liveness check fails (8/8 green with the widened window); the cleaner variant samples liveness first and the ready-file second (race-free by ordering: a process dead at sample time wrote its ready-file earlier). Also exposes test "N=4 ... admission cap 1" (no-shard describe). RC-C (orphan :339 in CI; seen locally 1 in ~700 runs; symptom PROVEN, bash-internal trigger NOT proven) - Step 1.7 create/migrate drain. CI run 38265950635 attempt 1 (shard 1/3, loadavg 11.11): the captured output ends "/home/runner/work/letflow/letflow/scripts/test_parallel.sh: line 554: finished_pid: unbound variable" then "preserving ...". Status was 1 so "assert status == 1" passed and the =~ "exceeded TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S=2s" failed because the script never reached Step 2 (nothing to do with the watchdog). "wait -n -p finished_pid" returned without setting the variable and set -u aborted at the lookup create_pid_to_partition[$finished_pid] (both the in-loop site ~L533 and the drain site ~L554). Same message reproduced once locally (scenario B, no load). A deterministic micro reproduction of the bash behaviour was not obtained (fg commands/sleep between jobs did not trigger it), so the exact bash trigger is a hypothesis; the fix does not depend on it. This one can hit REAL CI runs of every backend shard (it is in the create burst), not just stub tests, so it is the most valuable of the four. RC-D (diag :247 "huge" case; PROVEN from the CI log) - fixed wall-clock window in a test. CI run 38235738863 attempt 1: failing assertion `"...approx tests finished: 4" in mine`; the DIAG tail ends at P1-199971 (200000 expected), i.e. the awk stub (200k lines, 11 MB) had not finished writing when the 2 s watchdog (TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S=2) fired under load. Test-only. The "marked" case has the same shape with a much larger margin (64 lines in 2 s). Also: `elapsed < (@timeout_s + 15) * 1000` includes emission time. ======== FIX DESIGN ======== Production script (scripts/test_parallel.sh), 3 minimal edits: S1 (RC-A) define _tp_main_pid=$$ immediately before "trap cleanup_tmp_dir EXIT" (the mktemp line ~508); in cleanup_tmp_dir, directly after "local exit_code=$?" (that statement MUST stay first), add: [ "${BASHPID:-$$}" = "$_tp_main_pid" ] || return 0. Comment cites ISS-1062 and the fork-window mechanism. S2 (RC-B) in poll_template_ready_dir sample liveness FIRST into a local (alive=1; kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || alive=0), then: if [ -e ready ] -> ready; elif [ "$alive" -eq 0 ] -> ERROR, exit 1. Error text, the "see $tmp_dir/partition-N.log" reference and the bounded 0.2 s poll unchanged (the orphan EXIT-trap test pins "exited during its own template build"). S3 (RC-C) both "wait -n -p finished_pid" sites: set finished_pid="" before each wait; after "wait -n -p finished_pid; finished_exit=$?", if finished_pid is empty fall back: scan "${!create_pid_to_partition[@]}", for the first pid with ! kill -0 "$p" do `wait "$p"; finished_exit=$?; finished_pid=$p` (wait on an already-collected pid returns its saved status in bash; the script's own Step 3 relies on the same); if none is dead yet, sleep 0.05 and retry. Factor the two duplicated blocks into one function (reap_one_create). Also treat a pid missing from the map as "ignore and retry". Tests. New file test/scripts/test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs (async: false, @moduletag :tmp_dir; same bash()/launcher/Letflow.Test.TestParallelEnv.port_env scrub as the shard test, which test_parallel_env_guard_test requires; share the harness via test/support if preferred). Deterministic seam with no production change: BASH_ENV pointing at a shim file (non-interactive bash sources it; functions shadow builtins): T1 (RC-B) shim: kill() { if [ "$1" = "-0" ]; then command sleep 0.4; fi; builtin kill "$@"; }. Run shard 2/3 with TEST_PARALLEL_MAX_CONCURRENT_TEMPLATE_BUILDS=1. Assert status 0, 4/4 reported, no "exited during its own template build". Old script: exit 1 with that message. T2 (RC-C) shim: wait() { if [ "$1" = "-n" ] && [ ! -e "$SHIM_FLAG" ]; then : > "$SHIM_FLAG"; return 127; fi; builtin wait "$@"; } (first wait -n returns 127 with the variable untouched = the observed symptom). Assert status 0, 4/4 reported, no "unbound variable", and that the flag file exists (no vacuous pass). Old script: exit 1 "finished_pid: unbound variable". Variant: a create stub exiting 3 for one partition must still be reported as "ecto.create/ecto.migrate failed with exit 3". T3 (RC-A) shim: sleep() { if [ "${BASHPID:-$$}" != "$$" ] && [ "${1:-}" = "$SHIM_WATCHDOG_S" ]; then eval "$(trap -p EXIT)"; exit 0; fi; command sleep "$@"; } with TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S=$SHIM_WATCHDOG_S (a value no other sleep uses, e.g. 241). It re-arms the inherited trap inside the watchdog subshell and leaves with status 0, which is exactly what bash does in the fork window. Assert status 0, "4/4 partitions reported", the nested letflow_test_parallel.* dir still holds partition-1..4.log, no "No such file". Old script: the subshell runs cleanup with $?=0 and rm -rf's the dir -> missing logs, exit 1. All three: do NOT set TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS; keep @run_limit_ms 120_000 and the Port-collect bound. Failure-time capture (all test files that drive the script; one shared helper failure_context(tmp, out)): on assertion failure the message = script output + a listing of every file under tmp (File.ls_r) + full contents (capped 200 lines each) of every partition-*.log, create-*.log, calls.log, ready.log, db.log, build.log, + elapsed ms; "(nested tmp dir missing)" when the dir is gone, which would have identified RC-A on the first occurrence. The script already preserves tmp_dir on every nonzero exit and names "$tmp_dir/partition-N.log" in its error; the helper makes the CI log self-sufficient (acceptance 2: no new script knob needed, and TEST_PARALLEL_KEEP_LOGS must stay unset, see RC-A note). Implement as with_context(tmp, out, fn -> ... end) rescuing ExUnit.AssertionError and reraising with message <> context. The ready-file-to-global-index assertions (:241/:274) are unchanged; the wait stays bounded (script poll + @run_limit_ms). ======== PER-TEST TABLE (test/scripts/test_parallel_*_test.exs; the *.sh harnesses are not run by ExUnit) ======== shard_test: all describe cases (1/3, 2/3, 3/3, TOTAL/OFFSET, "SHARD wins" :274, no-shard default cap, 11 invalid-input cases) | window: none of its own, stubs instant; log read right after kill | failure: RC-A logs missing, RC-C unbound finished_pid | fix: S1 + S3, failure_context, T3/T2. shard_test "shard 2 of 3 under admission control cap 1" (:241) and "no shard env admission cap 1" | window: gap between -e and kill -0 in the poll | failure: "exited during its own template build" | fix: S2, T1. watchdog_diag "hung partitions: each DIAG block..." (marked) | window: stub must emit 64 lines + dots before the 2 s watchdog; "running for" asserted in 2..12 s | failure: truncated tail / wrong K | fix: W1 premise-checked escalation + failure_context. watchdog_diag "huge partition log" (:247, CI-confirmed) | window: awk emission of 200k lines before 2 s; elapsed bound includes emission | failure: tail ends P1-199971, K != 4 | fix: W1 (+ optional W2 faster writer). watchdog_diag "normal quick run prints no DIAG" | window: T=2 s on a run that takes ms (theoretical starvation > 2 s) | failure: spurious DIAG | fix: TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S=600 for this case (it asserts the absence of a firing watchdog). orphan "success" / "failing partition" / "EXIT-trap path" | window: assert_no_orphan_sleep runs ps immediately after exit; the group-killed sleep can still be listed for ms | failure: "orphaned watchdog sleep survived" on a loaded host; RC-A/RC-C also apply | fix: poll ps every 100 ms up to 5 s until no survivors, assert after the deadline with the last listing. orphan "Step 3 reaps a finished partition watchdog" (staggered) | window: stub 1 sleeps 2 s, stub 2 counts "sleep T" at a fixed 6 s (4 s margin) | failure: false count 2 under starvation | fix: stub 2 polls the count every 100 ms up to 30 s and records the first value 1 (or the last value at the deadline); the test still asserts 1 so a real orphan still fails. orphan "hung partition: watchdog still TERMs it" (:339, CI-confirmed RC-C) | window: stub hangs 600 s, T=2 s, bound 60 s: fine | failure: script aborted in Step 1.7 before any watchdog existed | fix: S3, failure_context; assertions unchanged. instrumentation_test (all) | window: stub sleeps 2 s; asserts secs >= 1 (epoch delta, safe) and <= 60 | failure: only RC-A/RC-C | fix: none of its own, covered by S1/S3. env_test / env_guard_test | no process timing | none. W1 premise-checked escalation (no assertion weakened): stubs write a sentinel $STUB_DIR/emitted-

AFTER their last output line (marked: after P

-LAST; huge: after the "...." line). Helper run_until_premise(tmp, env): attempts with T in [2, 6, 20]; the premise is "every partition's DIAG tail contains its final marker line (P

-LAST / ....)" i.e. emission finished before the watchdog fired. If the premise fails the attempt is discarded (fresh tmp subdir, same assertions) and the next, longer T is used; failure at the last T is reported with failure_context. Every existing assertion (tail window, exact K, 300 col cap, one host block, elapsed bound with T = the attempt's value) is kept; "host too slow" becomes a retry instead of a red build; worst case 2+6+20 s per case. ======== STRESS PROTOCOL (ELIXIR-DEV / TEST-RUNNER; mix only under the mutex, one acquisition per iteration) ======== 1. Per touched file set, 5 consecutive runs under load: start 8 busy loops (bash: for i in 1..8; do (while :; do :; done) & done; kill in a finally), then 5x [ acquire mutex; LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test mix test test/scripts/test_parallel_shard_test.exs test/scripts/test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_orphan_test.exs test/scripts/test_parallel_instrumentation_test.exs --seed <5 different seeds> ]; record the real ExUnit result lines and elapsed. Run one file first to learn whether test_helper needs the DB (stubs do not); start the throwaway postgres:16 on 5499 only if it does. 2. Script-level soak, no mix, no mutex: the stub harness used for this diagnosis in a linux container with 12 busy loops, >= 300 iterations per scenario (A: shard 2/3 cap 1, B: shard 1/3 cap 4) against the fixed script: expect 0 failures (baseline unfixed: B 1/300 logs-missing, A 0/150). The shims T1-T3 are the deterministic proof, the soak is the regression net. Harness (disposable, not committed): scratchpad h.sh of this session; recreate from the stub in write_stubs. 3. Fail-first: run the new race regression file against the unmodified scripts/test_parallel.sh and record 3 red tests (T1, T2, T3), then green on the fix. ======== MUTANTS (throwaway worktree, revert and verify) ======== MU-A1 remove the BASHPID guard in cleanup_tmp_dir -> T3 red. MU-A2 guard compares the wrong scope (e.g. [ "$BASHPID" = "$PPID" ]) -> T3 red. MU-B1 restore the -e-then-kill -0 order (no re-test) -> T1 red. MU-B2 keep liveness-first but drop the error branch (never fail) -> orphan "EXIT-trap path" red (needs exit 1 + message), so the fix cannot be neutered into an unbounded wait. MU-C1 delete the empty-finished_pid fallback -> T2 red. MU-C2 fallback that does not wait the pid (status lost) -> T2 variant with a failing create stub (exit 3) red. MU-D1 (diag) premise check always true -> a deterministic case: stub that sleeps 3 s before emitting at T=2 must be retried and end green; with the retry removed it is red. MU-O1 (orphan) remove the Step 3 "kill -- -watchdog" line from the script: "Step 3 reaps ..." red with count 2 and "success" red with "survived" (proves the polled ps still detects real orphans). MU-F (capture) delete the failure_context append: a deliberate probe test asserts the failure message contains partition-1.log content and the tmp listing. ======== RISKS ======== R1 S3 fallback busy-waits at 50 ms; harmless (create burst takes seconds). R2 BASH_ENV shims also load in the stub bash and launcher bash; they only define functions; the stubs call none of kill/wait/sleep. On git-bash the BASH_ENV path must be POSIX (cygpath -u, as the launcher does for PATH). R3 T3 relies on trap -p printing the parent's trap inside a subshell (verified on bash 5.2.37 linux; same on MSYS 5.2.37). R4 RC-C bash trigger unproven: T2 simulates the symptom, it does not reproduce the trigger; S3's fallback is trigger-agnostic. R5 CI bash may differ from 5.2.37 (ubuntu-latest moves to 26.04 on 2026-10-19): S1-S3 are version-independent by construction. R6 failure_context must not raise on a missing dir. R7 S1-S3 change a script every CI shard runs: run full mix letflow.check.test once on the fix branch, and the test_parallel_*_test.sh harnesses (not ExUnit-run) by hand. R8 wall-clock escalation in W1 adds up to 28 s per diag case in the worst case. Anti-pattern candidate (DOC-UPDATER): an instantly-exiting test double turns a benign check-then-act order and an inherited EXIT trap into live races; never assert a fixed wall-clock window against a process that must finish emitting first.
result.verdict: ROOT_CAUSES_CONFIRMED: RC-A (EXIT trap rm -rf in watchdog subshell, shard :274), RC-B (ready-file/kill -0 TOCTOU, shard :241), RC-C (wait -n -p leaves finished_pid unset, orphan :339), RC-D (stub emission vs 2 s watchdog, diag :247)
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design (S1-S3 script edits, race regression file with BASH_ENV shims T1-T3, failure_context helper, W1 premise-checked escalation for diag cases, orphan polling), then CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR
